title: How to parallax with rpg maker xp

posts.author: NaMosca
posts.body:
How parallax with rpg maker xp?​
So guys, I have a problem, in XP the tile is 32x32, I multiply it by the width and height of the map but it's not working, and even if I take a print directly from the game screen it doesn't work either, when using the panorama option the image is in the wrong position.
Neste caso, tento paralaxe a parede, mas ela fica na posição errada
but in the photoshop its seens ok

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
you'll need a script to change the parallax behaviour.
parallax mapping is a technique that was only developed after VX due to the extremely reduced mapping options in there and had not become natively supported until MV.

Well I didn't knew that, ty but unfortunately I didn't find any script but I find this tutorial that seems to work:
https://mundo-maker.foroactivo.com/t15993-xptutorial-parallax-mapping
so I can do this:
Since I want to take a screenshot to edit in the image editing program to make parallax in RPG Maker XP, for small maps that fit entirely on the screen I just need to take a screenshot of the screen and crop it in an editing program. For larger maps I'm thinking of it this way: if I find out the size of the map that fits on the screen, I can create several small maps in RPG Maker XP that fit entirely on the screen, take a screenshot of each one of them and put them all together in a single large map in the editing program, then I need to find a way to convert the size of the image that I created in the editing program to the number of tiles used in the height and width (because in RPG Maker XP to create a map you specify the number of tiles for width and height). I think it's just a matter of dividing the height and width of the image size by 32, because if I'm not mistaken an RPG Maker XP tile is 32x32. And then I create a map of that size, and then I assemble it in the editing program, I cut the image into parts to assemble a tileset and apply it to the RPG Maker XP map.
I can just create the hole map at image editor and then transfor it in a tileset and create a map at rpg maker xp with the right size
